literal: Of the three matters none is accomplished; even in defense one may not be secure—how can you first strike and attack others?
idiomatic: "Of the three, none is accomplished—even defense may be unsafe. How can you strike first and attack others?"

literal: They will surely hear our empty sound and grow strict; we also take their strictness and move—each pushes the blame, both thinking they respond to the enemy.
idiomatic: "They will hear our empty alarm and grow strict; we take their strictness and move—each pushes blame, both thinking they respond to the enemy."

literal: In the art of war one should divide calamity and meet the baleful qi—you must not act.
idiomatic: "In the art of war one should divide calamity and meet the baleful qi—you must not act."

literal: The emperor could not defy the multitude and followed the ministers' plan.
idiomatic: The emperor could not defy the multitude and followed the ministers' plan.

literal: Hao again stubbornly debated and was not followed.
idiomatic: Hao argued again but was not heeded.

literal: They then sent the Prince of Yangping Du Chao to garrison Ye and the Prince of Langye Sima Chuzhi and others to camp at Yingchuan.
idiomatic: They then sent Prince of Yangping Du Chao to garrison Ye and Prince of Langye Sima Chuzhi and others to camp at Yingchuan.

literal: Thereupon the raiders came swiftly; Dao Yanzhi entered the river from Qingshui,
idiomatic: The raiders then came swiftly. Dao Yanzhi entered the river from Qingshui,

literal: sailed upstream west, divided troops to hold the south bank, west to Tong Pass.
idiomatic: sailed upstream west, divided troops to hold the south bank, and reached Tong Pass.

literal: The emperor heard Helian Ding and the Song were dividing Hebei and first campaigned against Helian.
idiomatic: Hearing that Helian Ding and Song were dividing Hebei, the emperor first campaigned against Helian.

literal: The ministers all said: "Yilong's army is still in the river; leave them and go west—the prior foe cannot be surely taken;
idiomatic: The ministers all said, "Yilong's army is still on the river. Leave them and march west—the foe ahead cannot be surely taken."

literal: yet if Yilong seizes the opening, the eastern provinces will be lost."
idiomatic: "Yet if Yilong seizes the opening, the eastern provinces will be lost."

literal: The emperor was doubtful and asked Hao for a plan.
idiomatic: The emperor hesitated and asked Hao for counsel.

literal: Hao said: "Yilong and Helian Ding share the same evil and are linked, recruiting Feng Ba, drawing the Rouran, scheming rebellious hearts, singing to each other in emptiness.
idiomatic: Hao said, "Yilong and Helian Ding are joined in the same evil, recruiting Feng Ba, drawing the Rouran, scheming rebellion, singing empty encouragement to each other."

literal: Yilong waits for Ding to advance; Ding waits for Yilong ahead—neither dares enter first.
idiomatic: "Yilong waits for Ding to advance; Ding waits for Yilong ahead—neither dares enter first."

literal: In your servant's view they are like chickens linked by a cord, unable to fly together, and cannot harm.
idiomatic: "In my view they are like chickens tied by a cord, unable to fly together, and cannot harm us."

literal: Your servant at first thought Yilong's army would halt in the river, with two routes north: the eastern route toward Jizhou, the western route against Ye.
idiomatic: "I first thought Yilong's army would halt on the river with two routes north—the eastern toward Jizhou, the western against Ye."

literal: If so Your Majesty should campaign in person and could not advance slowly.
idiomatic: "If so Your Majesty would need to campaign in person and could not advance slowly."

literal: Now it is not so: east and west they array troops; within two thousand li no place has more than a thousand—form divided, momentum weak.
idiomatic: "Now it is not so. East and west they array troops; within two thousand li no post holds more than a thousand—form divided, momentum weak."

literal: From this view the weaklings' intent appears: they only hope to hold the river and defend, escape death as fortune, with no intent to cross north.
idiomatic: "From this the weaklings' intent appears: they only hope to hold the river, escape death as fortune, with no intent to cross north."

literal: Helian Ding's remnant root is easy to break; strike him and he will surely fall.
idiomatic: "Helian Ding's remnant root is easy to break; strike him and he will surely fall."

literal: After Ding is secured, east out of Tong Pass, sweeping forward, awe shaking the southern pole—north of the Jiang and Huai not a blade of grass will stand.
idiomatic: "After Ding is crushed, march east out of Tong Pass, sweep forward, and awe will shake the southern pole—north of the Yangtze and Huai not a blade of grass will stand."

literal: The sage stratagem alone issues—not what the foolish and near can reach; I beg Your Majesty to act without doubt."
idiomatic: "The sage stratagem issues alone—not what the foolish and near can grasp. I beg Your Majesty to act without doubt."

literal: When Pingliang was pacified, that day at the banquet the emperor took Hao's hand to show the envoy of Meng Xun, saying: "The Lord Cui of whom I spoke—this is he.
idiomatic: When Pingliang was pacified, at the banquet that day the emperor took Hao's hand to show Meng Xun's envoy, saying, "The Lord Cui I spoke of—this is he."

literal: His talent and stratagem have no peer today.
idiomatic: "His talent and stratagem have no peer today."

literal: My comings and goings I must ask; success and failure he decides—as if tally and seal matched."
idiomatic: "My every move I must ask him; success and failure he decides—as if tally and seal matched."

literal: Later Champion General An Li's army returned and presented southern captives; he therefore reported the southern bandits' words, saying: "Song charged its generals: if northern troops move, before they arrive go straight into the river.
idiomatic: Later Champion General An Li returned with southern captives and reported the enemy's words: "Song charged its generals: if northern troops move, enter the river before they arrive."

literal: If they do not move, halt at Pengcheng and do not advance."
idiomatic: "If they do not move, halt at Pengcheng and do not advance."

literal: As Hao had measured.
idiomatic: It was as Hao had measured.

literal: The emperor said to the ministers: "You before said my using Hao's plan was wrong and in terror firmly remonstrated.
idiomatic: The emperor told the ministers, "You said my following Hao's plan was wrong and remonstrated in terror."

literal: The ever-victorious house thinks itself far beyond others; at the end they still cannot match him."
idiomatic: "The ever-victorious think themselves far beyond others; in the end they still cannot match him."

literal: Hao was transferred to Minister of Education.
idiomatic: Hao was made Minister of Education.

literal: At the time the adept Qi Xian memorialized establishing four kings named for east, south, west, and north of the sun, wishing to bring auspicious fortune and remove calamities and anomalies.
idiomatic: At the time the adept Qi Xian memorialized establishing four kings named for the sun's east, south, west, and north, wishing to bring fortune and remove calamities.

literal: An edict ordered Hao to debate with the scholars.
idiomatic: An edict ordered Hao to debate with the scholars.

literal: Hao said: "The former kings founded the state to make frontier screens; one should not borrow names for fortune.
idiomatic: Hao said, "Former kings founded the state to make frontier screens; one should not borrow names for fortune."

literal: The sun and moon turn and circle the four directions; the capital dwells within them.
idiomatic: "The sun and moon turn and circle the four directions; the capital dwells within them."

literal: The title of four kings in fact covers the imperial domain; to name it is rebellious and cannot be accepted."
idiomatic: "The title of four kings in fact covers the imperial domain; to name it is rebellious and cannot be accepted."

literal: Earlier Xian had memorialized changing Dai to Wannian; Hao said: "In the past the Grand Ancestor Emperor Daowu received the mandate in his season, opened and expanded the great enterprise; all he established followed antiquity.
idiomatic: Earlier Xian had memorialized changing Dai to Wannian. Hao said, "Grand Ancestor Emperor Daowu received the mandate in his season and opened the great enterprise; all he established followed antiquity."

literal: Because he was first enfeoffed on the soil of Dai, he later was called Wei.
idiomatic: "Because he was first enfeoffed on the soil of Dai, he later was called Wei."

literal: Therefore Dai and Wei were used together, like Yin and Shang.
idiomatic: "Therefore Dai and Wei were used together, like Yin and Shang."

literal: The state's accumulated virtue is recorded in the histories; it should enjoy ten thousand myriads—one need not borrow a name for increase.
idiomatic: "The state's accumulated virtue is recorded in the histories; it should enjoy endless ages without borrowing a name for increase."

literal: What Xian has heard is all not righteous."
idiomatic: "What Xian proposes is all unrighteous."

literal: The emperor followed this.
idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

literal: At the time the King of Hexi Juqu Mujian harbored divided loyalty; the emperor was about to campaign against him and first asked Hao.
idiomatic: At the time Hexi king Juqu Mujian harbored divided loyalty. The emperor was about to campaign and first asked Hao.

literal: Hao replied: "Mujian's wicked heart is already exposed—he cannot fail to be executed.
idiomatic: Hao replied, "Mujian's wicked heart is already exposed—he must be executed."

literal: When the official army campaigned north in years past, though it did not capture all, in truth there was no harm.
idiomatic: "When the official army campaigned north in years past, though it did not capture all, in truth there was no harm."

literal: At that time those who marched, inner and outer army horses, were three hundred thousand head; counting dead and wounded on the road, not full eight thousand.
idiomatic: "At that time inner and outer forces mustered three hundred thousand horses; dead and wounded on the road numbered fewer than eight thousand."

literal: Each year lean deaths are constant, never less than ten thousand—thus not less than before.
idiomatic: "Each year lean deaths alone are constant, never fewer than ten thousand—not less than the campaign's toll."

literal: Yet distant lands heard the empty report and thought the great loss meant they could not rise again.
idiomatic: "Yet distant lands heard empty report and thought the great loss meant we could not rise again."

literal: Now strike them unawares; the great army arrives suddenly—they will surely be terrified and in turmoil, not knowing what to do, and capture is certain."
idiomatic: "Strike them unawares now. The great army arrives suddenly—they will be terrified and in turmoil, not knowing what to do, and capture is certain."

literal: Mujian is young and weak; his younger brothers are arrogant and unrestrained, contending for power across the realm; hearts are divided and scattered.
idiomatic: "Mujian is young and weak; his brothers are arrogant, contending for power; hearts are divided."

literal: Moreover in recent years heaven's disasters and earth's changes have all been in Qin and Liang—a state ripe for destruction."
idiomatic: "Moreover in recent years heaven's disasters and earth's changes have all fallen in Qin and Liang—a state ripe for destruction."

literal: The emperor ordered the ministers to debate; Prince of Hengnong Xi Jin and more than thirty others all memorialized, saying: "Mujian is a western frontier petty state; though his heart is not that of a pure vassal, he succeeded his father in maintaining tribute and the court received him with frontier ritual.
idiomatic: The emperor ordered debate. Prince of Hengnong Xi Jin and more than thirty others memorialized, "Mujian is a western frontier petty state. Though not a pure vassal at heart, he succeeded his father in tribute and the court received him with frontier ritual."

literal: Moreover a royal princess was sent in marriage; the crime is not very clear—we say only to keep him on a loose rein.
idiomatic: "A royal princess was sent in marriage; his crime is not glaring—we say only to keep him on a loose rein."

literal: Now horses and men are weary and should rest a little.
idiomatic: "Horses and men are weary and should rest a little."

literal: Moreover their land is brackish and barren, almost without grass and water; when the great army arrives it cannot long halt.
idiomatic: "Their land is brackish and barren, almost without grass and water; when the great army arrives it cannot long halt."

literal: When they hear the army comes they will surely complete walls and hold the city; attack is hard to pull down and in the wild there is nothing to seize."
idiomatic: "When they hear the army comes they will complete walls and hold the city; attack is hard and the wild offers nothing to seize."

literal: Then Director Gu Bi, Li Shun, and the rest all said: "From west of Wen Gate River to Liangzhou the land is pure dry stone, utterly without grass and water, no flowing streams seen.
idiomatic: Then Director Gu Bi, Li Shun, and the rest said, "From west of Wen Gate River to Liangzhou the land is pure dry stone, utterly without grass, water, or flowing streams."

literal: All say south of Guzang city on Tianti Mountain winter snow piles one zhang deep; by spring and summer it melts and flows down to form a stream drawn for irrigation.
idiomatic: "All say south of Guzang on Tianti Mountain winter snow piles one zhang deep; by spring and summer it melts, flows down, and is drawn for irrigation."

literal: When they hear the army comes they will break this channel mouth so water does not flow and bring thirst and exhaustion.
idiomatic: "When they hear the army comes they will break the channel so water does not flow and bring thirst and exhaustion."

literal: Within a hundred li of the city is red earth without grass—cannot long station horses and men.
idiomatic: "Within a hundred li of the city is red earth without grass—it cannot long support horses and men."

literal: Jin and the rest's plan is right."
idiomatic: "Xi Jin and the rest are right."

literal: The emperor then ordered Hao to use his former words and debate sharply with Jin together.
idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Hao to take his former argument and debate sharply with Xi Jin.

literal: The others had no further words and only said there was no grass or water there.
idiomatic: The others had no further argument and only repeated that there was no grass or water.

literal: Hao said: "The Treatise on Geography in the Book of Han says 'The livestock of Liangzhou are the richest under heaven'—if there were no grass and water, how could they pasture?
idiomatic: Hao said, "The Book of Han's Treatise on Geography says, 'The livestock of Liangzhou are the richest under heaven.' Without grass and water, how could they pasture?"

literal: Moreover Han people dwell there—they would never build walls and cities and establish commanderies and counties on land without grass and water.
idiomatic: "Han people dwell there—they would never build walls, cities, commanderies, and counties on land without grass and water."

literal: Moreover when snow melts it can barely gather dust—how could it open channels and draw irrigation for millions of qing?
idiomatic: "When snow melts it can barely wet dust—how could it open channels and irrigate millions of qing?"

literal: This talk greatly slanders men."
idiomatic: "This talk grossly slanders the truth."

literal: Li Shun and the rest again said: "We ourselves have seen it—how can we debate together?"
idiomatic: Li Shun and the rest said again, "We have seen it with our own eyes—how can we debate together?"

literal: Hao said: "You all received men's gold and wish to speak for them—you think because my eyes do not see I can be deceived!"
idiomatic: Hao said, "You received men's gold and wish to speak for them—you think because I did not see it I can be deceived!"

literal: The emperor listened hidden, heard this, and came out to see Jin and the rest in person.
idiomatic: The emperor listened in secret, heard this, and came out to see Xi Jin and the rest in person.

literal: His words were stern and severity showed in his bearing.
idiomatic: His words were stern and severity showed in his face.

literal: The ministers then dared speak no more.
idiomatic: The ministers then dared speak no more.

literal: They then campaigned against Liangzhou and pacified it.
idiomatic: They then campaigned against Liangzhou and pacified it.

literal: Grass and water were abundant, as Hao had said.
idiomatic: Grass and water were abundant, as Hao had said.

literal: An edict then ordered Hao to oversee historical affairs, striving for truthful records.
idiomatic: An edict then ordered Hao to oversee historical affairs and strive for truthful records.

literal: He then supervised secretariat affairs, with Palace Secretariat Attendant Gao Yun and Palace Cadet Zhang Wei participating in composition, continuing the former chronicle.
idiomatic: He supervised secretariat affairs, with Palace Secretariat Attendant Gao Yun and Palace Cadet Zhang Wei joining the compilation to continue the former chronicle.

literal: As for additions and subtractions, praise and blame, weighing and polishing, Hao was master.
idiomatic: Additions, subtractions, praise, blame, weighing, and polishing were all in Hao's hands.

literal: Hao had discernment and took human relations as his charge.
idiomatic: Hao had discernment and took human relations as his charge.

literal: In the eras of Mingyuan and Taiwu the state sought worthy talent within the seas, raising men from humble places.
idiomatic: In the eras of Mingyuan and Taiwu the state sought worthy talent across the realm, raising men from humble places.

literal: Worthy men of foreign and distant lands obtained and employed—all were through Hao.
idiomatic: Worthy men from foreign and distant lands obtained and employed—all came through Hao.

literal: As for ritual, music, statutes, and regulations, all looked to Hao as their source.
idiomatic: Ritual, music, statutes, and regulations all looked to Hao as their source.

literal: When Jingmu first held the hundred offices, Hao again assisted in government with Prince of Yidu Mu Shou.
idiomatic: When Jingmu first held the hundred offices, Hao again assisted government with Prince of Yidu Mu Shou.

literal: They were again about to campaign against the Rouran; Liu Jie again raised objections.
idiomatic: They were again about to campaign against the Rouran; Liu Jie again objected.

literal: The emperor wished all the more to campaign and summoned Hao to ask.
idiomatic: The emperor wished all the more to campaign and summoned Hao.

literal: Hao replied: "In the past campaign against the Rouran, the army was not many days out when Jie and the rest each wished to return.
idiomatic: Hao replied, "In the past campaign against the Rouran, the army had not been out many days when Jie and the rest each wished to return."

literal: Later they obtained a letter from the enemy saying when the army returned it was thirty li from the bandits—that was Jie and the rest's plan gone too far.
idiomatic: "Later we obtained an enemy letter saying when the army returned it was thirty li from the bandits—that was Jie and the rest pushing the plan too far."

literal: The northern lands have much accumulated snow; in winter they always avoid cold and migrate south.
idiomatic: "The northern lands hold much snow; in winter they always flee cold and migrate south."

literal: If you use that season and march the army out secretly, you will surely meet them.
idiomatic: "Use that season, march the army out secretly, and you will surely meet them."

literal: Once you meet them, you can capture them."
idiomatic: "Once you meet them, you can capture them."

literal: The emperor thought it so.
idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

literal: They then divided the army into four routes; the generals all met at Luhun Sea.
idiomatic: They divided the army into four routes; the generals all met at Luhun Sea.

literal: The day of meeting was fixed, but Jie, resenting that his plan was not used, discouraged and misled the generals, and returned without merit.
idiomatic: The rendezvous day was fixed, but Jie, resenting that his plan was not used, discouraged and misled the generals, and they returned without merit.

literal: The emperor toured west to East Yong, personally came to Fenqu, viewed the rebel Xue Yongzong's ramparts, and advanced the army to besiege them.
idiomatic: The emperor toured west to East Yong, came personally to Fenqu, viewed rebel Xue Yongzong's ramparts, and advanced to besiege them.

literal: Yongzong sent troops wishing to fight; the emperor asked Hao: "Can we strike today?"
idiomatic: Yongzong sent troops to fight. The emperor asked Hao, "Can we strike today?"

literal: Hao said: "Yongzong does not know Your Majesty has come in person; men's hearts are secure and firm.
idiomatic: Hao said, "Yongzong does not know Your Majesty has come in person; his men's hearts are secure."

literal: The north wind is swift; you should strike urgently and in a moment you will surely break them.
idiomatic: "The north wind is swift. Strike urgently and you will break them in a moment."

literal: If you wait until tomorrow, fearing they see the official army's grandeur, they will surely flee by night."
idiomatic: "Wait until tomorrow and, seeing the official army's grandeur, they will flee by night."

literal: The emperor followed this; Yongzong collapsed and was destroyed.
idiomatic: The emperor followed this counsel; Yongzong collapsed and was destroyed.

literal: The imperial carriage crossed the river; the vanguard reported bandits on the north bank of the Wei.
idiomatic: The imperial carriage crossed the river; the vanguard reported bandits on the north bank of the Wei.

literal: The emperor reached Luoshui Bridge; the bandits had already fled by night.
idiomatic: The emperor reached Luoshui Bridge; the bandits had already fled by night.
